newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Guitar Center,NeoMagic debut strong.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Guitar Center,NeoMagic debut strong.

text.p: Initial public offerings on Friday met strong demand as Wall Street drove up prices for shares of Guitar Center Inc, a chain of guitar retail stores, and NeoMagic, which makes multimedia accelerators for personal computer (PC) notebooks.
IPO analysts had expected moderate premiums because the deals were attracting even finicky institutional investors, wary of both high prices and low quality balance sheets.

Shares of Agoura Hills, California-based Guitar Center rose 1-5/8 to 16-5/8 with more then 2.5 million shares traded at midday. The offering was for 6.75 million shares which priced at $15 each, in the middle of their estimated pricing range of $14 to $16. Goldman Sachs was the lead underwriter of the IPO, which raised roughly $100 million.

Of the total number of shares offered, 5.4 were offered in the United States and 1.35 million were offered internationally. Other underwriters of the offering were Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, Montgomery Securities, Dain Bosworth, and Chase Securities Inc.

NeoMagic shares jumped more than fifteen percent at their market debut with solid gains of up 2 to 14 in early afternoon trading. Morgan Stanley was the lead underwriter of the offering, which was in strong demand.

The company offered three million shares which priced well above their first price range of $7 to $9. The range was raised to $9 to $11 as demand picked up and the shares finally priced even higher on Thursday, as $12 a share.
